identity.name: Duchy of Croatia
native_names: Regnum Chroatorum (Latin, 'Realm of the Croats', Trpimir's charter wording)
Dux Croatorum (Latin, 'Duke of the Croats', the Branimir inscription of 888)
alt_names: Duchy of Dalmatia and Liburnia (Borna's title)

land.text: the infobox 'Preceded by: Byzantine Empire; Avar Khaganate' without saying which land came from which

predecessors.note: The page ('c. 614 the Avars and Slavs sacked ... Salona') gives no hand-over year or boundary; Cliopatria's first shape (741) is used for both predecessors.

land.text: the infobox 'Preceded by: Byzantine Empire; Avar Khaganate'

predecessors.note: No page opened dates the Croats' leaving Avar rule. Cliopatria's Avar Khaganate row (561-805) touches this shape 741-792 (seed neighbours).

land.text: Cliopatria's last shape of the duchy (922-925): the duchy elevated to a kingdom, 'Elevation to kingdom: c. 925'

successors.note: The Duchy page: Tomislav 'last duke' 910-925, 'regarded as first king'; the Tomislav page: crowned 'in 924 or 925'. The kingdom-of-croatia dossier starts in 925 and adds Sisak and part of the former Pannonian duchy, so this dossier ends in 924 to hand over without an overlapping year.

capitals.name: Nin
capitals.note: The infobox says 'No permanent capital. Seats were Klis, Solin, Knin, Bijaći and Nin.' The Borna page: Fine (1991) says Borna 'resided at Nin' (undated, c. 810-821). The years 741-809 and 822-844 are a default, no page places a seat then (Mislav, before c. 845, 'ruled from Klis' on the Duchy page).

capitals.name: Klis
capitals.note: The Trpimir page: Trpimir, c. 845, took power and made Klis his seat (the Duchy page has Mislav already ruling from Klis). Later dukes used Knin, Solin and Biaći (infobox seats; Trpimir's 852 charter and the 892 charter of Muncimir were issued at Biaći near Trogir). Domagoj is 'a Knin nobleman'. No page gives the seat year by year.

rulers.name: Borna
rulers.note: Infobox 'Borna: 810-821 (first known duke)'; 'Duke of the Guduscani' (818), 'Duke of Dalmatia' (819), 'Duke of Dalmatia and Liburnia' (821), a vassal of the Franks. Died 821, succeeded by his nephew Vladislav (no dates for Vladislav, Ljudemisl or Mislav, so the strip has a gap 822-844).

rulers.name: Trpimir I
rulers.note: 'from around 845 until his death in 864'; first duke of the infobox's Trpimirovic dynasty (845-1091).

rulers.name: Domagoj
rulers.note: 'Duke of Croatia from 864 to 876'; usurped the throne; founder of the Domagojevic.

rulers.name: Zdeslav
rulers.note: The Duchy page: after Domagoj's death in 876 'Zdeslav ... returned from exile'; the Domagoj page has him return from Constantinople in 878; the Branimir page has him killed near Knin in 879. Years disputed between pages.

rulers.name: Branimir
rulers.note: 'reigning from 879 to c. 892'; papal recognition 7 June 879.

rulers.name: Muncimir
rulers.note: Came to the throne 'c. 892'; named 'Duke of the Croats' in the Biaći charter of 28 September 892. The end year is not given by any page opened; 909 is inferred from Tomislav's 910.

rulers.name: Tomislav
rulers.note: Duke 'c. 910', 'mentioned as duke of Croatia in 914'; the infobox gives 910-925, king from 924 or 925 (see kingdom-of-croatia).

keyframe_review.note: unverified: the page dates no Croat duchy to 741-787 ('Established in the 7th/8th century'; its only 741-775 reference is gold coins of Constantine V found in archaeological contexts), and the Borna page quotes Novakovic's doubt that Dalmatian Croatia was a duchy at the start of the 9th century. Kept as drawn: 21,088 km2, bbox 14.26-17.11 E, 43.54-45.43 N, the coast from Liburnia to the Cetina. Every Cliopatria shape of this state is the same Dalmatian coast and hinterland, 78-79 H3 cells (about 19,700-20,000 km2 on the grid; 20,690-21,530 km2 in shapes.csv). The page gives no infobox area, so no area check is possible (the Wikipedia article describes extent in regions only).

unverified, as for 741: the same 79 cells, 21,018 km2. Cliopatria's Lombard kingdom touches it 751-774 (seed neighbours); the page says only that in 788 Charlemagne, 'after conquering Lombardy', subjugated Istria. No infobox area.

788-792: 2 cells (506 km2) differ from the 751 shape on the northern edge; grid noise, no event. The page: 'In 788 Charlemagne ... subjugated Istria', next door to the shape's north-western corner. 20,690 km2; no infobox area.

793-805: identical to 788 on the grid. The page: 'The Franks gained control of Pannonia and Dalmatia in the 790s and the first decade of the ninth century'; infobox 'Frankish vassalage: 790s'; 'In 799, the Franks under ... Eric of Friuli were defeated in the Battle of Trsat in Liburnia' (inside the shape's north-west); 'from 803 Frankish rule was recognized in most of northern Dalmatia'. The duchy is therefore a Frankish vassal from the 790s or 803; the vassal_start belongs in the kingdom-of-the-franks ledger (see notes). 20,760 km2; no infobox area.

New keyframe for 806-849, which Cliopatria leaves empty; its Kingdom of the Franks row (806-849) covers all 79 cells of the duchy instead (checked with the gazetteer: 79 of 79 cells in 806 and 78 of 78 in 840). The pages keep the duchy alive: 'From c. 810 Borna ruled most of northern Dalmatia and was a vassal of the Carolingian Empire' (Duchy page); Borna is 'Duke of Dalmatia and Liburnia' in 821; the Pax Nicephori page: in 812 'Dalmatian Croatia was confirmed as Frankish, with the exception of the Byzantine cities and islands'; Vladislav 821, Mislav, then Trpimir 'around 845'. The shape is the 805 shape unchanged (the 850 shape is the same within one cell); 806-809 rests on the 803 sentence and continuity, not on a dated page. The kingdom-of-the-franks dossier carries these cells as a gain at 806 (confidence 1); they should be a vassal_start there, not a second owner.

correction.text: the duchy of Borna, Vladislav, Mislav and Trpimir under Frankish overlordship: 'most of northern Dalmatia' with Liburnia, without the Byzantine coastal cities and islands (812)

keyframe_review.note: 850-875: 78 cells, 20,876 km2, the same land. Trpimir (c. 845-864): 'Realm of the Croats' in his charter of 4 March 852 (disputed: 'about 840' on the Duchy page), seat Klis, 'in 846, Trpimir successfully attacked the Byzantine coastal cities'; the Duchy page has him repel a Bulgarian invasion 854-860. Domagoj 864-876. The page names no territory gained or lost, so the shape is unverified in extent. No infobox area.

876-881: 79 cells (one more than 850, 253 km2, grid noise). Domagoj 'razed four Frankish Cities in Istria in 876' (a raid, Istria not held) and 'soon after eliminating the Frankish suzerainty, Domagoj died in 876'; the Branimir page: 7 June 879 papal recognition 'as a sovereign state', sovereignty from Carolingian and Byzantine rule. Zdeslav, 'a noted Byzantine vassal' in 878 (Theme of Dalmatia page), ruled between. 20,946 km2; no infobox area.

882-886: Branimir, 'reigning from 879 to c. 892'; he 'retained its sovereignty from both Carolingian and Byzantine rule'. Dalmatian cities under Byzantine protection paid him 710 ducats in tribute (undated, 'in Branimir's time'). One cell fewer than 876; grid noise. 20,690 km2; no infobox area.

887-895: Branimir named 'Dux Croatorum' on the Muc altar beam of 888; Muncimir 'c. 892' and, on the Duchy page, 'Duke of the Croats' in the Biaci charter of 28 September 892. The page names no land change; 20,946 km2 on the same cells. No infobox area.

896-897: identical to 887 on the grid. Late 9th century: 'the Hungarians crossed the Carpathians' and defeated Braslav of Pannonia; no page dates a Hungarian attack on Croatia in these years. 20,760 km2; no infobox area.
898-899: identical to 887 on the grid, 20,946 km2. The page gives nothing for these years. No infobox area.
900-910: 78 cells, 20,876 km2, the same land. 'Croatia also waged battles with the Magyars during the early 10th century' (no year, no place). No infobox area.

911-921: 3 cells (759 km2) added on the south-eastern edge (16.61-16.95 E, 44.80-44.93 N; two of them lie in Cliopatria's East Franks 900 shape, so a boundary artefact) and 2 dropped in the north: no event. 21,530 km2, the largest of the row. The Tomislav page (duke c. 910, 'mentioned as duke of Croatia in 914') says 'during the early 10th century, Croatia was divided into 11 counties' (Livno, Cetina, Imotski, Pliva, Pset, Primorje, Bribir, Nona, Knin, Sidraga, Nin) and 'probably grew beyond these', without locating them; Livno and Pliva suggest land east of this shape. Extent unverified; the expansion into Pannonia and Bosnia is undated on the page and is left to the kingdom-of-croatia dossier (925). No infobox area.

922-925, shape unchanged, years cut to 922-924: the kingdom-of-croatia dossier carries 925 (new keyframe, 'crowned in 924 or 925'), so this dossier ends in 924 to avoid two owners in one year. The shape is 6 cells (1,517 km2) smaller than 911 on the eastern edge (16.52-16.95 E, 43.72-44.93 N), 3 of them inside Cliopatria's Principality of Serbia 922 shape; the Tomislav page says only that the Bulgarians destroyed Serbia in 924 and Serbian refugees fled to Croatia, so the loss is recorded at confidence 1. 20,873 km2; no infobox area.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 922 shape unchanged for 922-924; 925 belongs to the Kingdom of Croatia

ledger.note: 741: the Croat duchy appears on the Dalmatian coast and hinterland. Page silent on a founding year: infobox 'Established in the 7th/8th century', 'preceded by the Byzantine Empire; Avar Khaganate'; 741 is Cliopatria's first year and the page's only date from 741-775 is the gold coins of Constantine V.

region.text: the Guduscani (Lika, 'along the river Gacka') and the Kupa river where Borna met Ljudevit

ledger.note: 819: Ljudevit's army meets Borna's on the Kupa and 'the Guduscani abandoned Borna and crossed to Ljudevit's side'; in December Ljudevit 'raided Dalmatia' and retreated in the winter. The Kupa battle is autumn 819 on the Ljudevit page; the zone (Lika and the Kupa valley) is the researcher's reading of 'Guduscani ... Lika' and 'on the Kupa river'. Borna allied with the Emperor at Aachen in January 820 and died in 821.

region.text: the Guduscani (Lika, 'along the river Gacka') and the Kupa river where Borna met Ljudevit

ledger.note: 822: Ljudevit flees from Sisak to the Serbs before 'the last and final Frankish invasion of 822'; the page gives his death only as 823 in the lead and says Ljudemisl of Dalmatia killed him.

c. 845: Trpimir I succeeds Mislav and the Trpimirovic line begins (infobox: 'ruled by the Trpimirović and Domagojević dynasties 845–1091'). The state, its land and its colour continue; the page names no dynasty for Borna (810-821), Vladislav or Mislav.

c. 845: the seat moves to Klis (Trpimir 'ascended the throne in Klis and expanded the early Roman stronghold into Klis Fortress, the capital of his domain', Trpimir page). The Duchy page says Mislav already ruled from Klis, so the move may be earlier; before 845 the default seat is Nin, where Borna 'resided' (Borna page).

864: Domagoj usurps the throne. 'In 864 Duke Domagoj, founder of the House of Domagojevic, usurped the throne after the death of Trpimir' and drove out Trpimir's sons; the duchy continues under a new dynasty.

region.text: 'Dalmatian cities under Byzantine protection' that paid tribute; Zadar and Split are the researcher's reading, the page names no city

ledger.note: 879: the Byzantine-protected Dalmatian cities pay Croatia tribute. 'Dalmatian cities under Byzantine protection paid 710 ducats of tribute to the Croatian ruler' is dated only 'in Branimir's time' (reign 879-c. 892); 879 is the reign's first year, the cities named are the researcher's guess.

c. 892: Muncimir 'came to throne after the death of Branimir (c. 892)' and 'returned power to the Trpimirovic dynasty'; the duchy continues. The Biaci charter of 28 September 892 names him 'Duke of the Croats'.

region.text: the eastern strip (16.52-16.95 E, 43.72-44.93 N, 6 cells) that Cliopatria's 922 shape no longer holds

ledger.note: 922: page silent. Cliopatria's shape loses 6 cells (1,517 km2) on the eastern edge, 3 of them inside its Principality of Serbia 922 shape and 2 inside the Kingdom of Croatia 926 shape. The Tomislav page has only 'In 924 ... the Bulgarians destroyed the Principality of Serbia' and refugees fleeing to Croatia. A gap for a gap-filler.

region.text: 'Dalmatian cities under Byzantine protection' that paid tribute; Zadar and Split are the researcher's reading, the page names no city

ledger.note: 924: the tribute is closed at the hand-over to the kingdom; no page says when it ended. The Theme of Dalmatia page has 'Around 923 AD, Tomislav of Croatia ... transferred the control of the Byzantine Dalmatian cities to the new Croatian kingdom', while the Tomislav page finds 'no evidence' that Byzantium recognised the loss of its rights in the theme; the kingdom-of-croatia dossier follows the first.

region.text: the whole duchy, elevated to a kingdom

ledger.note: c. 925: the duchy becomes the Kingdom of Croatia under Tomislav. 'Elevation to kingdom: c. 925'; infobox: Tomislav 'last duke' 910-925, 'regarded as first king'; the Tomislav page: 'crowned in 924 or 925', place and officiant unknown. 924 is used so the kingdom (found 925) does not overlap.

wars.name: Battle of Trsat and the Frankish conquest of Liburnia
wars.outcome: The Franks under Eric of Friuli were defeated at Trsat in Liburnia in 799, yet 'from 803 Frankish rule was recognized in most of northern Dalmatia'; the 812 Pax Nicephori confirmed Dalmatian Croatia as Frankish and left the coastal cities and islands to Byzantium.
wars.note: The page names only the Frankish side of the Trsat battle; the Croat side is the researcher's reading. No ledger contest is recorded because the page names no ground held by either side; Trsat (Rijeka) lies at the shape's north-west corner.

wars.name: Ljudevit's revolt

zones.text: the Guduscani (Lika, 'along the river Gacka') and the Kupa river where Borna met Ljudevit

wars.outcome: Ljudevit, duke of the Slavs in Lower Pannonia (810-823), rose against the Franks in 819, beat Borna on the Kupa when the Guduscani deserted, and raided Dalmatia in December 819; the Franks invaded from several sides in 820 and 822 and Ljudevit fled from Sisak to the Serbs in 822.
wars.note: The principality-of-lower-pannonia dossier starts in 838, after this revolt, so the counterpart is named by its ruler. The Ljudevit page notes that 'Duke of Pannonian Croatia' is an erroneous, anachronistic title.

wars.name: Trpimir's war with the Byzantine coastal cities
wars.outcome: 'In 846, Trpimir successfully attacked the Byzantine coastal cities and their patricius' (the strategos of Zadar); no city is recorded as taken.
wars.note: The Trpimir page dates the victory over the patricius to 846 as well.

wars.name: Bulgarian invasion of Croatia under Boris I
wars.outcome: 'Between 854 and 860, he [Trpimir] successfully defended his land from the Bulgarian invasion'; a peace followed.
wars.note: The Trpimir page dates the repulse of Boris I's army to 854 only. The fetched summary placed the invasion in north-eastern Bosnia, outside Cliopatria's shape; no ground changed hands.

wars.name: Venetian-Croatian wars (Tradonico to Domagoj)
wars.outcome: Venice attacked the eastern Adriatic coast including Croatia in 839; Domagoj was 'forced to make an unfavourable peace with Venice' in 865; Zdeslav 'restored peace with Venice in 878'.
wars.note: The 865 peace is from the Domagoj page, which adds undated attacks by Domagoj's navy on Venetian ships in the Gulf of Piran and a failed attack on Grado. No land moved.

wars.name: Croatian raid on Frankish Istria
wars.outcome: 'The Croatian forces razed four Frankish Cities in Istria in 876' (Umag, Novigrad, Sipar and Rovinj); Domagoj died in the same year 'soon after eliminating the Frankish suzerainty'.
wars.note: A raid; Istria was not held, so no zone. The Domagoj page adds that in 875 Louis the German's Franks 'tried to reassert their authority in Dalmatia'.

wars.name: Croatian-Magyar wars
wars.outcome: 'Croatia also waged battles with the Magyars during the early 10th century'; the Tomislav page says Croatia was not the Hungarians' primary target, which killed Braslav, the last duke of Lower Pannonia.
wars.note: The page dates nothing more exactly and names no place; the span is the researcher's bracket, hence no zone.

certainty.note: No survey line exists. The only treaty line, the 812 Pax Nicephori division between the Frankish-ruled Croat hinterland and the Byzantine coastal cities and islands, was 'unclear' by 817 (Leo V sent an embassy to Aachen 'to clarify the unclear Dalmatian boundaries'), so it is soft too. The northern and eastern frontiers (Pannonia, Bosnia) are unattested by any page opened.

notes:
Dossier written 2026-11-01 from 9 pages (the page budget for 13 shapes). Cliopatria row 'Duchy of Croatia' 741..925, 13 shapes, all the same ~79 H3 cells (the Dalmatian coast from Liburnia to the Cetina, about 20,000 km2), kept as one state; 12 of the 13 shapes are kept, 922 has its years cut to 922-924, and one new keyframe (806-849) fills a gap in Cliopatria. The start year 741 is Cliopatria's: the Duchy page gives only '7th/8th century'. The end is 924, not 925, so the kingdom-of-croatia dossier (found 925, with a 925 keyframe that applies the kingdom shape) does not overlap this one; flip to 925 if the orchestrator prefers an overlapping hand-over year.

Cliopatria conflict, 806-849: the Kingdom of the Franks row covers all 79 duchy cells in 806-849 and the kingdom-of-the-franks dossier records a confidence-1 gain at 806 (counterpart duchy-of-croatia, source Charlemagne page, which does not mention Croatia). The pages say the duchy continued under Borna, Vladislav, Mislav and Trpimir as a Frankish vassal; the new keyframe duchy-of-croatia_806 keeps it on the map. Mirror events for other dossiers (vassal events are written by the overlord, with the vassal as counterpart): kingdom-of-the-franks vassal_start duchy-of-croatia 803 (Duchy page: 'from 803 Frankish rule was recognized in most of northern Dalmatia'; infobox 'Frankish vassalage: 790s') and vassal_end 876 (Domagoj page: 'Soon after eliminating the Frankish suzerainty, Domagoj died in 876'; the Duchy page puts the revolt after the 871 Bari campaign; the Branimir page says 'free of Frankish suzerainty' in 879), with the 806 gain removed; byzantine-empire vassal_start duchy-of-croatia 878 and vassal_end 879 (Theme of Dalmatia page: 'in 878 AD, Zdeslav of Croatia was a noted Byzantine vassal'; Branimir kills the Byzantine supporter Zdeslav in 879); papal recognition 7 June 879 (Branimir page) has no ledger type here and is only in the 876 keyframe note.

Disagreements between pages: Zdeslav returns 876 (Duchy page) or 878 (Domagoj page), killed 879 (Branimir page); Trpimir's charter 4 March 852 or 'about 840' (Duchy page); Bulgarian invasion 854-860 (Duchy page) or 854 only (Trpimir page); Klis as Mislav's seat (Duchy page) or Trpimir's (Trpimir page); the Theme page has the Byzantine Dalmatian cities transferred to Croatia c. 923, the Tomislav page finds no evidence Byzantium recognised any loss, and Fine, quoted on the Tomislav page, excludes the Byzantine towns from the realm; the 812 treaty is the Pax Nicephori, headed 'Peace of Aachen' on that page. A first guess 'Borna,_Duke_of_Croatia' for the Borna URL returned not-found; the page is Borna_of_Croatia (opened).

Events at confidence 1 (page silent): 741 found, 879 tribute start, 922 loss, 924 tribute end. The 788, 850-911 shape differences are 0-3 cells (0-760 km2) and are grid noise, with no event. The Tomislav expansion into the former Pannonian duchy including Sisak and into northern and western Bosnia is undated on the page and is carried by the kingdom-of-croatia dossier at 925; if it happened 910-924 the duchy's 911 and 922 shapes are too small. Not settled: the extent of the duchy before the 790s (no page; Novakovic doubts a duchy before the 9th century); the 11 counties' places; the Narentines (Pagania) and the Neretva are on none of the pages opened, and Zachlumia appears only as a possible vassal of Tomislav (Tomislav page, 925 council).

Counterparts needing dossiers: Ljudevit's Lower Pannonia 810-823 (the principality-of-lower-pannonia dossier starts 838; a separate rebel/state dossier or a change of its start is needed); the Narentines/Pagania (Neretva) 9th-10th century; Zachlumia (Hum); the Byzantine Dalmatian cities (Theme of Dalmatia) inside byzantine-empire. Gazetteer: no unknown names are used in region specs; Nin, Klis, Knin, Bijaci (Biaci), Sisak, Trsat and the Kupa are absent from places.jsonl/rivers.jsonl (capitals above carry coordinates).
